page: Amazon Web Services c9g.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AWS Graviton ARMv9 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz using the Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture, with 8.0 GB of system memory. The instance utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and operates on the arm64 architecture. It includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.57 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.45 GB/sec. Passmark memory testing also places the instance in the top tier with a score of 3281.9. However, its Passmark CPU score of 5622.45 and CPU encryption score of 1184.98 are categorized as weak. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 8025.08 and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaching 68.74 GB/sec. Large block memory read bandwidth is measured at 122.33 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is 42.49 GB/sec.

The instance is designed for compute-bound workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. It is suitable for web serving, with a static web serving throughput of 14.88 GB/sec, and database operations, processing 13.06 million Redis SET operations per second. For machine learning, it handles small-model LLM inference at average speeds, but performance drops to a poor rating for medium-model prompt processing. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which represents a key architectural tradeoff.

The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. In benchmark testing, the c9g.xlarge delivers top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, alongside a top-tier Passmark memory score. Conversely, its Passmark CPU and encryption scores are weak. This instance is suited for web serving, database operations, and lightweight single-threaded processing tasks, though its memory-to-CPU ratio and lack of local storage require careful workload planning.
